title: Lipid profile and lipid lowering therapy in patients with lower extremity arterial disease
summary:
Lower extremity arterial disease (LEAD) has a significant impact on the health and quality of life of patients. In particular vasoconstriction and vascular deposits can increase the risk of serious cardiovascular events such as heart attack, stroke and cardiovascular death.
Early diagnosis and appropriate therapeutic measures are crucial to alleviate the symptoms and prevent the disease from progressing. Lowering low-density lipoprotein cholesterol (LDL-C) is considered one of the most important therapeutic strategies for improving the cardiovascular prognosis. 
However, it has been shown in everyday clinical practice that patients with LEAD are very poorly treated, especially with regard to lipid-lowering medications. Particularly in patients with a high risk of cardiovascular diseases, it is important to control lipid levels and lower them to a certain individual range, as recommended in the guidelines for the treatment of
LEAD; this applies above all to LDL-C.

The aim of this study is to investigate the effects of structured strengthening and follow up of patients and the training of patients´ family doctor with regard to the individual LDL-C
target values of high-risk patients. For this purpose, a program was developed in which the patients in the treatment group (empowerment group) are given monthly support by a specially trained member of the study management team to ensure that patients take their medication regularly or to find out what the difficulties are if this does not happen. In addition, the patients´ family doctor should also be informed about their patients' laboratory values and the importance of achieving the LDL-C target values and the possibilities of lipid-lowering medication should be discussed. This should raise awareness among patients and their treating physicians of compliance with the target values and ultimately lead to a lower risk of dying from cardiovascular disease or to a better quality of life.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
1. Signed and dated informed consent of the subject 
2. Confirmed diagnosis of LEAD
3. LEAD stage Rutherford 1-5
4. No peripheral revascularization within the next 4 weeks
Exclusion criteria:
1. Acute limb ischemia
2. LEAD Rutherford stage 6
3. Life expectancy less than 12 months
